secops-guide-steps.statement: The Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for Identity Protection in the SecOps platform has five steps: Set Up Your Account (sign-in credentials arrive by email once the organization is provisioned), Configure Users & Roles, Assess the Security Threats, Monitor Threats Using Dashboards and Reports, and Remediate Identity Risks.

quotes: Step 1: Set Up Your Account
After your organization is provisioned for the Agentic Security Operations Platform (SecOps Platform),
you will receive an email at your registered email address with a username and password to sign in to the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal.
Step 2: Configure Users & Roles
Step 3: Assess the Security Threats
Step 4: Monitor Threats Using Dashboards and Reports
Step 5: Remediate Identity Risks

secops-guide-assess-workflow.statement: The SecOps guide's assess workflow is: evaluate overall findings on the Findings Overview dashboard (categorized by severity, type, affected tenants, identity providers, remediation ease, exploitability and impacted assets), then view users, tenants, identity findings and alerts.

quotes: Evaluate overall findings.
The Findings Overview dashboard provides a high-level view of the identity findings and their overall security posture in your organization.
Findings are categorized by severity, type, affected tenants, identity providers, remediation ease, exploitability, and impacted assets.
View a list of users.
View a list of tenants.
Assess identity‑related security risks.
Review the alerts associated with identity findings.

what-it-is.statement: Identity Protection detects anomalous activity such as compromised credentials, suspicious logins and sensitive data theft, and gives continuous, unified visibility into identity risks; its architecture page calls it an identity threat detection and response (ITDR) solution integrated with the SecOps platform.

quotes: It detects anomalous activities such as compromised credentials, suspicious logins, sensitive data theft, etc., and provides continuous and unified visibility into identity risks.
Identity Protection is an effective identity threat detection and response solution (ITDR) integrated with the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform.

secops-part.statement: It is part of the Zscaler SecOps platform and works alongside UVM, AEM and SOC Workbench.

quotes: Identity Protection is part of the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform and works alongside Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM), Asset Exposure Management (AEM), and Security Operations Center (SOC) Workbench

features.statement: Its listed features are detecting identity risks (compromised accounts, suspicious sign-ins, leaked credentials, authentication anomalies), containing identity attacks, fixing weak passwords, exposed credentials and excessive privileges, a single identity view across sources, and custom dashboards and reports.

quotes: Detect Risks Associated with Identities: Detect compromised accounts, suspicious sign‑ins, leaked credentials, and anomalies in authentication activities
Mitigate Identity Attacks: Detect and contain identity-based attacks before they can cause harm.
Strengthen Identity Posture: Find and fix weak passwords, exposed credentials, and excessive privileges.
Single Identity View: Unify identity data from disparate sources into one view.
Reports and Dashboards: Custom dashboards and reports to view specific results as required.

components.statement: Its key architecture components include an Identities App in the SecOps platform for management and analysis, an ITDR Connector that streams ITDR data into the data fabric, the Data Fabric Cluster that processes raw data, and the Zero Trust Exchange, whose access policy controls block compromised users when an identity attack is detected.

quotes: Identities App: Built into the SecOps platform and serves as the central point of management and analysis for the Identity Protection service.
ITDR Connector: The data connector that serves as the source stream from the ITDR solution to the data fabric.
Data Fabric Cluster: The entire data fabric cluster responsible for processing raw data from various sources.
Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE): Identity Protection leverages the ZTE platform to mitigate risk with access policy controls that block compromised users when an identity attack is detected.

zte-containment.statement: Through the Zero Trust Exchange, access policy controls block compromised users when an identity attack is detected, and the ZIA and ZPA integration adds visibility, enrichment and containment.

quotes: Identity Protection leverages the ZTE platform to mitigate risk with access policy controls that block compromised users when an identity attack is detected.
Integration with Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Private Access (ZPA) provides better visibility, enrichment, and containment capabilities.

connectors.statement: Connectors ingest posture scans, change detections, alerts and identity records, and integrate with identity providers such as Okta and Microsoft Entra to consume identity data directly from the customer's IdP.

quotes: Identity Protection uses connectors to ingest data from sources such as posture scans, change detections, alerts, and identity records.
These connectors also integrate with identity providers like Okta and Microsoft Entra, enabling the system to consume identity data directly from the customer's IdP

ad-posture.statement: An AD posture scan targets a named AD domain and requires Zscaler Client Connector on a domain-joined Windows machine; it runs LDAP queries to map schema, users, computers, OUs and other objects, then checks them for misconfigurations and vulnerabilities.

quotes: You can configure an AD scan by specifying the AD domain you want to assess. For assessing the AD domain, Zscaler Client Connector must be installed on a domain-joined Windows machine.
Identity Protection audits an AD domain by running LDAP queries to build a map of schema, users, computers, OUs, and other objects in your identity store.
It then runs checks against these objects to find misconfigurations and vulnerabilities that exist in your AD domains.

entra-posture.statement: An Entra ID posture scan connects the Entra ID tenant and uses a deployment script that creates the needed resources there (resource group, app, storage account, service principal) and enables diagnostic settings to enable change detection using logs; the audit logs are analyzed and the results appear in the Identities app.

quotes: Identity Protection uses a deployment script to set up all necessary resources such as resource group, app, storage account, service principal, etc. in the Entra ID tenant.
Diagnostic settings are also enabled by the deployment script to enable change detection using logs.
The audit logs are analyzed, and the results are available in the Identities app.

okta.statement: The Okta integration enriches identity metadata, detects real-time changes on an Okta identity, and can act on it, for example activate or suspend a user or clear its sessions.

quotes: Identity Protection integrates with Okta to enrich the identity metadata, identify real-time changes on an Okta identity, and perform actions on an Okta identity like activate user, suspend user, clear user sessions, etc.

change-detection.statement: Identity change detection monitors critical changes in AD domains and Entra ID tenants in real time; in addition to real-time alerting it gives remediation guidance as video tutorials, commands and scripts.

quotes: Identity Protection provides real-time monitoring of critical changes in your AD domains and Entra ID tenants that introduce new risks
In addition to real-time alerting, you also get remediation guidance in the form of video tutorials, commands, and scripts that can be used to resolve issues.

credential-exposure.statement: The credential exposure scan checks endpoints for identity material stored locally, such as usernames, passwords, API keys, SSH keys and certificate files.

quotes: Credential Exposure Scan: Identity Protection scans endpoints to check for risky identity material, such as usernames, passwords, API keys, SSH keys, certificate files, and other credentials stored locally on endpoints.

threat-detection.statement: Identity threat detection is enabled as an endpoint policy on designated machines with Zscaler Client Connector installed; detectors such as DCSync, DCShadow and Kerberoasting are enabled through policies, and Client Connector signals Identity Protection when it sees a pattern.

quotes: Identity threat detection is enabled as an endpoint policy on designated machines with Zscaler Client Connector installed.
Security teams can enable detectors (DCSync, DCShadow, Kerberoasting, etc.) via policies on designated endpoints.
If a pattern is noticed, Zscaler Client Connector sends signals to Identity Protection indicating that a threat has been detected.

legacy-redirect.statement: Identity Protection is managed and fine-tuned through the SecOps platform, whose Settings page adjusts scan configurations with an explanation of each option; where deeper configuration is needed, some links redirect to the legacy ITDR experience.

quotes: Custom Configuration: Manage and fine-tune identity protection through the SecOps platform.
Within the Settings page, you can adjust scan configurations and review clear explanations for each option.
When deeper configuration is required, certain links redirect you to the legacy ITDR experience

risk-summary-widgets.statement: The Risk Summary dashboard shows a unified risk score of 0 to 100 (100 is critical) for a chosen AD domain and for a chosen Entra ID tenant, with the top 3 critical issues in each, plus the top 3 critical exposed endpoint credentials.

quotes: View a unified risk score of the AD domain on a scale of 0 to 100, where 100 is critical.
View a unified risk score of the Entra ID tenant on a scale of 0 to 100, where 100 is critical.
View the top 3 issues with critical severity that are found in the AD domain.
View the top 3 issues with critical severity that are found in the tenant.
View the top 3 exposed endpoint credentials with critical severity.

risk-summary-attack-mapping.statement: The Risk Summary dashboard maps risks to MITRE ATT&CK techniques on a kill chain, and its risk at-a-glance widgets list the top 10 AD users and computers and the top 10 Entra ID identities with the highest risks.

quotes: View all the risks mapped to MITRE ATT&CK exposure techniques and displayed on a kill chain.
View the top 10 users and computers that have the highest risks in the AD domains.
View the top 10 identities (users and service principals) that have the highest risks in the Entra ID tenants.

ad-threat-detection-filter.statement: The Active Directory Threat Detection filter applies this query to the Investigate dashboard, selecting itdr events and endpoint events with sub_type cbf and cbf.is_ad_decoy_credential true, or sub_type kerberoast or ad_enumeration.

quotes: The Active Directory Threat Detection filter applies the following query to the Investigate dashboard.
(type is "itdr") or (type is "endpoint" and ((sub_type is "cbf" and cbf.is_ad_decoy_credential is true) or (sub_type in ["kerberoast", "ad_enumeration"])))
To apply the Active Directory Threat Detection filter, click AD Threat Detection from the ITDR menu.

investigate-dashboard.statement: The Investigate dashboard shows all events generated by the Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal and can be filtered with built-in or custom queries.

quotes: The Investigate dashboard allows you to view and interact with all events generated by the Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal.
You can use the built-in queries or custom queries to filter the dashboard

change-check-cycle.statement: The what-is page says identity change detection checks run every 15 minutes from Zscaler Client Connector installed on the endpoints or landmine agents for the AD domain, and that detected changes are marked as having a good or bad impact.

quotes: These checks run every 15 minutes from Zscaler Client Connector installed on the endpoints or landmine agents for the given AD domain.
The changes detected are marked as having a good or bad impact.

scan-assignee-and-results.statement: The what-is page says an AD domain scan can be assigned to a Zscaler Client Connector or an endpoint agent, and after the scan the result is viewed on the Identity Posture dashboard, where the assessment results include a domain risk score, focus areas, a list of the riskiest users and computers, and MITRE ATT&CK kill chain mapping.

quotes: You can assign a Zscaler Client Connector or an endpoint agent to scan an AD domain for identity misconfigurations and vulnerabilities.
After the scan is complete, you can view the result on the Identity Posture dashboard.
The assessment results include a domain risk score for identity posture quantification and tracking, focus areas to prioritize remediation, a list of the riskiest users and computers
MITRE ATT&CK kill chain mapping for visibility into security blind spots

detector-examples.statement: The what-is page names DCSync, DCShadow, Kerberoasting, session enumeration, privileged account access and LDAP enumeration as examples of available threat detectors, and says the security team can use them to identify a threat on the designated endpoint.

quotes: Some of the available threat detectors include DCSync, DCShadow, Kerberoasting, session enumeration, privileged account access, LDAP enumeration, and more. The security team can use these threat detectors to identify a threat on the designated endpoint.

no-extra-agents-claim.statement: The what-is page lists as a benefit that ITDR integrates with Zscaler Client Connector to unlock new capabilities without the need for additional agents or virtual machines.

quotes: Integrates with Zscaler Client Connector to unlock new capabilities and protection without the need for additional agents or virtual machines (VMs).

setup-step-order.statement: The ITDR step-by-step configuration guide runs in this order: log in to the Admin Portal, configure users and roles, configure single sign-on, configure threat detection policies, integrate with Okta, assess AD posture, assess Entra ID posture, set up the endpoint credential exposure scan, analyze the assessment report, enable change detection, and remediate risky identities and changes.

quotes: Step 1: Log In to the Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal
Step 2: Configure Users and Roles
Step 3: Configure Single Sign-On Authentication
Step 4: Configure Threat Detection Policies
Step 5: Integrate ITDR with Okta
Step 6: Assess Your Active Directory Posture
Step 7: Assess Your Entra ID Posture
Step 8: Set Up Endpoint Credential Exposure Scan
Step 9: Analyze the Assessment Report
Step 10: Enable Change Detection
Step 11: Remediate Risky Identities and Changes

remediation-scope.statement: The ITDR step-by-step configuration guide says risky AD and Entra ID identities and bad changes can be remediated directly from the ITDR Admin Portal.

quotes: You can remediate risky AD and Entra ID identities and bad changes directly from the ITDR Admin Portal.

no-client-surface.statement: No vendored client covers Identity Protection or ITDR: the Go and Python SDKs, the Terraform providers, the Ansible collections, the MCP server, the OneAPI Postman collection and the captured Automate contract have no such service; the MCP server's ZIdentity tools manage users and groups, not identity risk.

quotes: used in your server-side code to interact with the Zscaler API platform across multiple products such as:

no-client-surface.conditions: Rests on an absence. The Python README's product list (introduced by the quoted line) names no Identity Protection API, and at the pins `git grep -i -E 'itdr|identity.protection'` finds no such code in the Go or Python SDKs, the ZIA, ZPA, ZCC or ZTC providers, the Ansible collections or the MCP server (the only hits are base64 test data); the Postman collection has no match.

change-detection-timing.summary: The architecture page describes change detection as real-time monitoring; the change detection articles describe near real-time visibility on a 15-minute cycle.

quotes: Identity Protection provides real-time monitoring of critical changes in your AD domains and Entra ID tenants that introduce new risks

positions.says: Identity Protection provides real-time monitoring of critical changes in AD domains and Entra ID tenants.

quotes: AD Change Detection uses the AD scan results to collect data. The scan runs every 15 minutes.
Obtain near real-time visibility into new misconfigurations and security risks introduced to your AD.

positions.says: AD Change Detection gives near real-time visibility, from an AD scan that runs every 15 minutes.

quotes: ITDR provides real-time monitoring of critical changes in your AD domains and Entra ID tenants that introduce new risks

positions.says: The page itdr-understand-zscaler-itdr-architecture (Understand the Zscaler ITDR Architecture) says ITDR provides real-time monitoring of critical changes in AD domains and Entra ID tenants.

change-detection-timing.impact: The pages give different descriptions of how quickly a change is detected (real-time against near real-time on a 15-minute cycle) and do not say how they reconcile.

risk-score-method.title: How the Risk Summary's 0 to 100 risk score is computed
risk-score-method.detail: The Risk Summary article says the unified risk score runs from 0 to 100 where 100 is critical, but does not state how it is computed from issues or severities.

api-and-legacy-parity.title: Identity Protection's API and connector-configuration surface, and its parity with legacy ITDR
api-and-legacy-parity.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the help portal lists ITDR under Zscaler Legacy, Identity Protection in the SecOps UI is the current generation, and advanced tasks redirect to the legacy ITDR experience; the authoritative API surface, connector configuration API, report or export API, and exact parity between the two are not identified. The current page confirms only the redirect for deeper configuration (legacy-redirect).
api-and-legacy-parity.blocks: telling an operator whether identity findings or scan configuration can be automated, and which console holds a given setting

credential-scan-agent.title: Whether the credential exposure scan requires Zscaler Client Connector on the endpoint
credential-scan-agent.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Credential Exposure Scan requires ZCC. The current architecture page describes the scan of endpoints but does not name the agent that runs it; the About Endpoint Credential Exposure Scan article it links is not captured.
credential-scan-agent.blocks: telling an operator what must be installed for endpoint credential findings to appear
